subject.title: [Bug] Sandbox validateEnvVarValue base64 heuristic false-positives on legitimate long alphanumeric values

question: Should the sandbox env sanitizer reduce base64-value warnings for non-credential-looking keys while preserving credential-name and null-byte protections?
rationale: The current behavior is noisy for legitimate values, but changing the heuristic narrows a defense-in-depth credential signal on a sandbox boundary.

options.title: Land the linked narrow heuristic fix
options.body: Accept the open PR's credential-name plus structured-base64 gate after sandbox/security review and use it to close this issue.

options.title: Keep the broader value-only warning
options.body: Retain the current noisy warning if maintainers prefer maximal credential-value detection over false-positive reduction.

options.title: Request a different security model
options.body: Ask for a revised PR that uses a separate explicit policy or audit path instead of changing the existing warning gate directly.

recommendation.title: Land the linked narrow heuristic fix
recommendation.body: Accept the open PR's credential-name plus structured-base64 gate after sandbox/security review and use it to close this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The sanitizer was introduced by steipete and this is a security-boundary behavior choice in that code path.
